text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today as crude oil prices surged to six-month highs on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude hit $116 per barrel—up sharply from earlier in the week—driven by reports of potential U.S. military action against Iran and existing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian infrastructure. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise, since higher oil sells at higher prices.

The broader tailwind is that geopolitical risk is reshaping energy markets in ways that favor U.S. oil and gas companies. News from the past two days shows the Iran conflict is not only pushing up crude prices globally but also redirecting energy investments toward American exporters—including natural gas suppliers. This regional instability, while creating real-world risk, is translating into higher energy company valuations.
